verses.1: His crest is his glory; who dares to lay hands on it?
verses.2: No one is bold enough to provoke him, for who can stand before me?
verses.3: Who has gone before me, that I should repay them? All that is under the heavens belongs to me.
verses.4: I will be silent on his behalf, and I will not speak of his might or his beauty.
verses.5: Who can strip him of his outer garment? Who could approach him with a double coat?
verses.6: Who can open the doors of his face? His teeth are terrifying around.
verses.7: His shields are proud, his scales are like a tightly sealed wall.
verses.8: One joins to the next, and no wind passes between them.
verses.9: They cling to one another, bound together and not to be separated.
verses.10: His sneezing flashes light, and his eyes are like the glint of dawn.
verses.11: Fire goes out from his mouth, like flaming torches, and sparks of fire leap out.
verses.12: Smoke goes out from his nostrils, like a boiling pot over a fire of coals.
verses.13: His breath ignites coals, and a flame goes out from his mouth.
verses.14: Strength lies in his neck, and death flees before him.
verses.15: His flesh is joined fast, and nothing can move it.
verses.16: His heart is as hard as a stone, and as firm as the lower millstone.
verses.17: When he rises, the mighty trees tremble, and the cedars of Lebanon fall.
verses.18: No sword can reach him, nor spear or dart.
verses.19: Iron is as chaff to him, and bronze as rotten wood.
verses.20: An arrow does not make him flee; he laughs at the shaking of a spear.
verses.21: Sharp rocks are as chaff to him; he treats the sea as a dry place.
verses.22: He treads upon the depths, as if they were a dry path; he makes the sea like a road of clay.
verses.23: He makes the deep boil like a pot, and the sea becomes like a pot of ointment.
verses.24: A path glows behind him, and he turns the abyss into a path for the old.
verses.25: There is nothing on earth like him, a creature made to be beyond the reach of my messengers.
verses.26: He sees all the lofty ones; he is king over all the sons of the chaos.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "His crest is his glory" — the Hebrew uses a wordplay between "crest" (מִזְרָח) and "glory" (כָּבוֹד), both derived from root *ZRCH*; the former is more literally "ornament" or "crest."
- v. 21: "He treats the sea as a dry place" — the Hebrew uses a metaphor of the sea being as nothing to him, akin to a dry, walkable path.
- v. 25: "beyond the reach of my messengers" — the Septuagint suggests "angels," but the Hebrew uses *mal'akhim* ("messengers"), which need not be angelic in this poetic context.
